# `prefer-range-for`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports an exact zero-based, unit-step counter `while` loop that a range `for`
expresses directly.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A range keeps the iteration space in one place and makes the index immutable.

## When it fires

The counter must be a `usize`, must not be changed in the body, and must not be
read after the loop. The proven rewrite is eligible for fix-all.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn run() void {
    var i: usize = 0;
    while (i < 10) : (i += 1) {
        step(i);
    }
}

fn step(i: usize) void {
    _ = i;
}
```
